name: rank-list
description: An ordered list where the position is the point — the reserved names board, a leaderboard, a queue. A real `<ol>`, because the numbering is data and not decoration: a `<div>` with a hand-typed digit in front of it loses its meaning the moment one row is filtered out.

rank.$description: Right-aligned and tabular in a fixed column, so 9 and 10 stack rather than shifting the name beside them. This is the whole reason it is a part and not a `::marker`: a marker cannot be given a width.

meta.$description: The one thing that varies down the list — a date, a status. A long list of identical rows is a long list of identical rows; something has to differ or the eye has nowhere to land while scrolling.

a11y.note: An `<ol>` with a label, so a screen reader says 'list, ten items' and can announce the position of each. The rank is inside the row rather than a `::marker` because it needs a fixed width — but it must stay INSIDE the `<li>` so the reading order is rank-then-name, not name-then-rank.
